claims.text: Stable protective-oxide formation above 900 °C in CrFeCoNiX alloys is governed by formation of a continuous, chemically compatible Cr-Al-rich sub-oxide layer.
Sufficient Al content promotes an adherent, slow-growing mixed chromium-alumina protective scale.
The proposed chromium-alumina scale minimizes thermal stress and oxygen ingress.
Higher Mn or Si contents promote defective oxides that are prone to cracking and spallation.
The starting material is a single- or multiphase metallic solid-solution CrFeCoNiX high-entropy alloy.
Arc melting followed by homogenization annealing is a suitable route for preparing the proposed alloys.
The baseline is a lower-Al and relatively Mn- or Si-richer alloy that forms unstable oxide layers.
Increasing Al relative to Mn or Si is the intervention proposed to improve protective-oxide formation.
The relevant exposure range is approximately 950–1000 °C for 100–200 hours in air, controlled oxygen partial pressure, or a mildly corrosive environment.
The proposed interfacial Cr-Al oxide sublayer has low defect density.
The proposed interfacial Cr-Al oxide sublayer has a thermal-expansion match with the alloy substrate.
Cr and Al oxides form rapidly during the proposed oxidation process.
Adequate Al enables development of a slow-growing, adherent alumina-based barrier.
The alumina-based barrier slows further oxygen ingress.
Oxide-substrate compatibility reduces thermal-mismatch stresses and thereby reduces cracking and spallation.
Al-richer alloys will develop thinner, more continuous, and more adherent high-temperature oxide layers than Mn- or Si-richer alloys.
Al-richer alloys will exhibit less oxide-scale cracking and spallation than Mn- or Si-richer alloys under identical exposure conditions.
The hypothesis is restricted to alloys that retain a single- or multiphase metallic solid-solution microstructure without significant segregation or secondary-phase formation.
Si and Mn may alter oxidation kinetics and thermal-stress development, potentially through interactions with Al content.
